subject: Business Models
title: Software Eating Subscriptions
description: A fast breakdown of Software Eating Subscriptions for builders.

hook.text: Peloton sells a $1,500 bike and charges $44/month for classes. Without the subscription, it's a coat rack.

buildup.text: Connected hardware companies use subscriptions to turn products into ongoing services.

discovery.text: Ring Doorbell now requires a $4/month subscription for video recording. The camera alone just shows real-time.

twist.text: John Deere requires a subscription for GPS guidance on tractors. Farmers are hacking their own equipment.

climax.text: Every hardware company wants recurring revenue. The line between product and service is dissolving.

punchline.text: Buy the hardware, subscribe to its brain. Everything is a service now.

quiz.question: Why are hardware companies adding subscription requirements?
options: To convert one-time sales into recurring revenue

details.summary: Industries from fitness to farming are being transformed as physical products and services add subscription software layers. Peloton charges monthly for streaming classes. John Deere charges farmers for GPS guidance software. Tesla charges monthly for autonomous driving features.
details.whyItMatters: Software subscriptions are being grafted onto nearly every physical product category, transforming one-time purchases into ongoing revenue streams. This shift changes the economics of hardware from commodity margins to recurring software margins.
takeaways: Physical products increasingly require software subscriptions for full functionality
Manufacturers add recurring revenue to one-time hardware sales
Customers face growing subscription fatigue from software-gated features

faq.question: Why are hardware companies adding software subscription layers?
faq.answer: Hardware margins are thin and one-time. Software subscriptions generate recurring high-margin revenue that investors value highly. Connected products enable feature gating and continuous value delivery. A $2,000 product generating $20 monthly creates $240 annual recurring revenue per unit.

faq.question: What is the consumer backlash against hardware subscriptions?
faq.answer: BMW charging for heated seats already built into the car drew widespread criticism. Consumers feel that paying for hardware should include its full capabilities. Printer subscriptions that disable cartridges if canceled anger users. The practice risks regulatory attention and brand damage.
